title: Oracle Browser Multi-Tab Lineage, Owner Labels, and Assistant Opening-Line Harvest
description: Add additive, backward-compatible browser provenance metadata and live ChatGPT tab harvest fields for the Oracle CLI repository. The implementation records a stable browser owner/agent label, keeps existing target/url/conversation matching intact, captures both first/opening and last assistant snippets, persists enriched harvest metadata, and displays lineage in oracle status --browser-tabs, oracle session <id> --harvest, and oracle session <id> --live.

userStories.title: Persist stable browser owner labels
userStories.description: As a multi-agent operator, I can map each Oracle browser run to a stable owner/agent label without changing existing tab matching.
acceptanceCriteria: Browser session metadata accepts optional browser.ownerLabel, browser.ownerSource, browser.runtime.ownerLabel, and browser.runtime.ownerSource fields.
Browser config accepts optional ownerLabel and derives a conservative default without requiring a new CLI flag.
Owner label resolution prefers explicit config, then env labels, then option/session slug, then cwd basename plus pid, then cwd basename, then pid, then session id.
Old meta.json files without owner fields continue to read and display without throwing.
Owner labels are provenance/display only and are not used as tab matching keys.

userStories.title: Capture first/opening and last assistant snippets
userStories.description: As an operator inspecting live ChatGPT tabs, I can see both the opening assistant text and the latest assistant text.
acceptanceCriteria: ChatGptTabSummary includes firstAssistantText, firstAssistantSnippet, openingLine, lastAssistantText, and lastAssistantSnippet.
Live tab inspection captures first/opening and last assistant snippets using current assistant-turn and answer fallback selectors.
Zero assistant turns produce empty first/opening/last assistant fields, not errors.
Existing target id, URL, and conversation id matching remains authoritative.
Stop-visible remains authoritative: if stopExists is true, active=yes and running state are preserved.

userStories.title: Persist enriched harvest metadata
userStories.description: As an operator harvesting detached browser sessions, I can persist owner and opening-line metadata for later inspection.
acceptanceCriteria: Harvest metadata persists ownerLabel, ownerSource, firstAssistantSnippet, openingLine, and lastAssistantSnippet under browser.harvest.
Harvest metadata remains backward-compatible with older browser.harvest objects.

Harvest output includes session id, owner when available, target id, conversation id, state, model, URL, assistant turn count, active/stop/send signals, opening/first snippet, last snippet, and last user snippet.
No eager metadata migration rewrites historical sessions.

userStories.title: Display tab lineage in status and live tail
userStories.description: As an operator watching multiple concurrent ChatGPT tabs, I can identify which session/owner each tab belongs to and what the first/latest assistant content is.
acceptanceCriteria: oracle status --browser-tabs displays target id, state, linked session id, owner when available, conversation id, active/stop/send signals, model, turn count, URL, opening/first snippet, and last snippet.
oracle session <id> --live status lines include session id, owner when available, target id, conversation id, state, active/stop/send signals, model, turn count, opening snippet, and last snippet.
Formatting remains compact and uses existing snippet truncation behavior.
Tests cover legacy owner fallback, harvest metadata shape, status-line provenance, and Stop-visible active behavior.
The implementation adds optional owner-label metadata without breaking old meta.json files.
The implementation captures and exposes first/opening and last assistant snippets for live ChatGPT tabs.
The implementation persists enriched harvest metadata through oracle session --harvest.
The implementation displays provenance and snippets through oracle status --browser-tabs and oracle session --live.
Stop-visible remains authoritative and active=yes behavior does not regress.
Focused tests pass for owner-label resolution, live tab extraction, CLI formatting, harvest persistence, config defaults, and legacy metadata compatibility.
pnpm run typecheck and pnpm run build pass.
nonGoals: Do not require a new CLI flag for owner labels in v1.
Do not use owner labels as tab matching keys.
Do not eagerly migrate or rewrite historical metadata.
Do not change ChatGPT submission behavior, model selection, conversation archiving, or Answer Now handling.
Do not loosen the existing Stop-button active-state rule.
testCommands: pnpm vitest run tests/browser/ownerLabel.test.ts tests/browser/liveTabs.test.ts tests/cli/browserTabs.test.ts tests/browser/config.test.ts

referenceImplementation.applyInstructions: Use Oracle's artifact as a candidate implementation and adapt it to the live repository. Do not blindly copy invalid JSON/code snippets; preserve the PRD acceptance criteria and existing repo patterns.
testCommands: pnpm vitest run tests/browser/ownerLabel.test.ts tests/browser/liveTabs.test.ts tests/cli/browserTabs.test.ts tests/browser/config.test.ts
assumptions: OpeningLine is best-effort and derived from the first assistant turn.
Existing target/url/conversation matching remains the source of truth.
No new CLI flag is required for v1 because env/slug/session fallbacks are sufficient.
knownRisks: ChatGPT DOM can flatten line breaks, so openingLine may equal the beginning of firstAssistantSnippet.
Remote and local browser paths must both propagate owner labels.
Status output can become noisy if snippets are not truncated.
rollbackNotes: All schema additions are optional; rollback can remove owner/opening display and persistence without breaking old metadata.
If DOM extraction regresses, revert liveTabs extraction changes while preserving owner-label fallbacks.
If status output is too noisy, keep harvest persistence and reduce status detail lines.
